reason: Feasibility/schedule lens: it survives. (1) No kernel code changes. --patch forkmid already exists (T6): FORKMID_ENABLE=0 is byte-identical, it is fail-soft ('FORKMID FAILED'), tests/test_forkmid.py covers it, and K3 is one builder line (CONTEXT l.1790). The amendment only touches the lab-side reading in tools/trainlab.py gates(). (2) The idea overstates its own change. gates() l.605-622 already audits forkmid on ALL lab clips with no SELECTION/CONFIRMATION split, and '0 TP per embryo' is the same as '0 TP pooled'. The real edits are: drop '>=3 FP, >=1 on 44b6'; add (c) FP>=1 and FP>TP; add (d) pooled adj_edge. aggregate() has no pooled-over-embryos key, so (d) needs ~10 lines or a post-hoc script. tests/test_trainlab.py l.446-461 asserts the old gate, so the new gate must be an ADDITIVE key. (3) Pre-registration timing is feasible and wider than the idea says. The exp60 kernel writes only dumps, so downloading the dumps reveals nothing. Fork labels and counts first appear at the local `python tools/trainlab.py score`. At 17:45 UTC no exp60 output exists locally (shard A pushed 17:15, ~2 h; shard B after FF). The deadline is therefore 'logged in CONTEXT with a UTC time before the first score run on any shard', which includes a partial shard-A run. This is the one real race, because the night plan has T9 running tonight. (4) Calendar: dumps ~19:15-20:30 UTC, local CPU scoring -> T9 26.09 ~02:00-09:00, then the K3 dummy (~0.5 GPU-h; ~5 h of quota left before the reset, 30 h after). S4 falls 26.09 10:00-13:00 with 7-8 h latency, so the score arrives ~18:00-21:00 26.09, well before R8 (27.09 12:00). S7 is the backup. Slots on 26.09 fit: K2, K3, K3b, K4. (5) Hidden-run cost is < 1 s/clip x ~100 clips, under 2 min against ~4 h of headroom. Caveats that do not refute it. (a) Retained clause (b), TP max mid <= 3.8 um, becomes the binding clause. exp39's 23 TP forks peaked at 3.76 um, and with ~15-25 new lab TP forks P(new max > old max) is ~n/(23+n) ~0.4-0.5. So P(pass) is ~0.35-0.5, not 0.6. (b) The lab control is x138 + safetail + dump-only insertion WITHOUT lowrefine. On the K2 dummy, lowrefine moves fork geometry: base forks >= 4.5 um go from 2/62 on exp56 to 1/61 on K2, and 2 new non-inserted forks appear. The lab therefore audits a slightly different coordinate regime than K3 ships, and the K3 dummy gate checks only the mechanics. (c) Governance: §e/§f say 'apply mechanically'. The T9 wording lives in TASK_CLOUD_SESSION, not verbatim in §e, whose S4 condition says only 'аудит E4 пройден'. The night standing OK covers the amendment only if it is logged before scoring and flagged to the user in the morning.
fix: Before ANY `trainlab.py score` run (shard A alone included), append a timestamped CONTEXT line: 'C04 audit amended (power): pass = 0 TP safe-division forks removed (pooled 56 clips) AND TP mid max <= 3.8 um AND removed evaluable FP >= 1 AND removed FP > removed TP AND pooled adj_edge delta >= -0.0002 AND nodes / inserted forks unchanged; the old T9 gate is still computed and reported, but S4 uses the amended one'. Implement it as an additive g['forkmid_v2'] in tools/trainlab.py gates(), with pooled summarise_rows over both embryos' forkmid45 vs control rows, so tests/test_trainlab.py stays green, and add one test for the new key. Freeze the 4.5 um threshold and clause (b) as they are, and do not relax (b) after seeing the data. Record in the report that the lab has no lowrefine, and add a K3-dummy log check that the forkmid_* counters are > 0 on 6bba_05db0fb1, so the removal path actually executes on the dummy. Then K3 = K2 + forkmid goes to S4 by R3, with S7 as the fallback.
realistic_gain: P(K3 ships forkmid) rises from ~0.08 to ~0.35-0.5, not 0.6, because clause (b) binds. Incremental EV is ~+0.0001-0.0002 public and ~+0.0001-0.0003 private, below one LB tick. It costs 0 hidden-run time, ~0.5-1 agent-hour and ~0.5 GPU-h for the K3 dummy, which the plan already needs.
